listenings.text: Hello, this is Claire Bennett from the London office. I am calling about the due diligence call on Thursday. I have already read your firm profile, and I have shared it with two colleagues here. Before we talk, I would like to understand your career trajectory a little better. How long have you worked in tax law, and when did you move from audit? I have also sent you three questions about the regulatory framework in Brazil. We have not agreed on the scope of the advisory mandate yet, so please follow up on that with my assistant. Thank you, and speak on Thursday.

Hi, it is Daniel from the tax team. Quick update before the client call. I have just finished the compliance review, and I have sent the memo to the client this morning. Two things. First, the reform milestone moved again, so the committee has not published the final text yet. Second, I carried out the impact analysis last week, and the tax exposure is lower than we expected. I have not spoken to the client about that yet, because I wanted us to be on the same page first. Can you call me before three o'clock? Thanks.

extra_audio.text: I started my career in audit, where I worked for four years. After that, I moved to a large bank and I learned how a bank really thinks. I joined my current firm in 2016, and a few years later I became a partner. Since then, I have led advisory mandates for banks and payment companies.

paras: Marcus Reid has worked in international tax for more than fifteen years. He started his career at a Big Four firm in London, where he spent four years in audit before he moved to tax. In 2014 he joined a boutique firm as a senior associate, and three years later the partners invited him to join them.

Since he became a partner, Marcus has led more than forty advisory mandates for banks, insurers and payment companies. He has carried out compliance reviews in six countries, and he has advised two investment funds on their tax exposure during a major reform. Last year he presented the firm's impact projections to a committee of foreign investors in Frankfurt.

Marcus has not finished his academic work yet. He completed a master's degree in 2019, and he has just applied for a doctoral program. His audit background, he says, still helps him every week: it taught him to read the numbers before he reads the opinions. He has never regretted the move from audit to tax, and he has already agreed to speak at the next reform milestone conference in October.
